meta.title: How It Works — RAG and loop agents in ShrimpPulse
meta.description: How ShrimpPulse works: Retrieval-Augmented Generation in version 2.0, the loop-agent architecture in development for 4.0, and what each does and does not guarantee.

hero.title: Two ways of answering a question
hero.lead: ShrimpPulse 2.0 answers by retrieving from a reviewed knowledge base before responding. ShrimpPulse 4.0 is being built as a loop agent that can retrieve, assess, and look again. This page explains both ideas briefly and without jargon, and is honest about what neither approach guarantees.

rag.title: What is a RAG chatbot?
paragraphs: RAG stands for Retrieval-Augmented Generation. A RAG chatbot does not answer purely from what its underlying language model remembers. It first searches a selected knowledge base for material relevant to the question, and then uses that material to formulate its answer.

A useful analogy is a librarian who, before replying, walks to the right shelf of an organised reference library, pulls the relevant pages, and answers with those pages open. The library in ShrimpPulse 2.0 is a pharmacological knowledge base that was curated and reviewed by an expert; the answers themselves are generated by the system each time, not individually reviewed.

Grounding an answer in retrieved information can improve its relevance and keep it close to the reviewed source material. It does not guarantee correctness: retrieval can miss the right passage, and the answer still has to be formulated well. This is one reason ShrimpPulse describes itself as decision support rather than a substitute for professional advice.

steps.title: Question
steps.text: A user asks about an antibiotic or chemical on LINE.

steps.title: Retrieve relevant knowledge
steps.text: The system finds the most relevant passages in the reviewed knowledge base.

steps.title: Formulate an answer
steps.text: An answer is written using the retrieved material and returned in the chat.

rag.flowNote: 2.0 uses a flow-agent approach: a defined sequence of steps with knowledge-base retrieval, which keeps responses predictable and fast.

loop.title: What is a loop agent?
paragraphs: A loop agent does not follow a single fixed sequence. At each step it can choose what to do next: retrieve information, use an available tool, or select a set of specialised instructions, called a skill, suited to the task at hand. It then assesses the result and decides whether it has enough to answer or needs to go around again.

In the architecture being developed for ShrimpPulse 4.0, this means the system can identify the type of question, select appropriate resources or skills, retrieve information in multiple steps, assess intermediate results, and seek further information when necessary. It is intended to connect related issues across disease, treatment, prevention, and farm conditions.

Consider a conceptual aquaculture situation. A farmer asks what to use for a problem in a pond. Rather than treating that as a product question, a loop agent can first consider which disease signs are present and what the pond conditions are, retrieve material on possible causes, assess whether the picture is clear, and only then move to treatment and prevention guidance, or suggest confirmatory testing if it is not. This describes an intended workflow in development, not a validated clinical process.

steps.title: Identify the question
steps.text: Recognise the type of question and select a suitable skill.

steps.title: Retrieve or use a tool
steps.text: Fetch relevant knowledge, possibly from more than one module.

steps.title: Assess the result
steps.text: Check whether the evidence gathered is sufficient.

steps.title: Answer
steps.text: Formulate the answer when the evidence is sufficient.

loop.loopLabel: Not enough evidence yet: go back and look further

skills.title: Antibiotic skills
skills.text: Responsible-use guidance drawn from the reviewed pharmacological knowledge base.

skills.title: Chemical skills
skills.text: Address factors such as efficacy, dosage, toxicity, and application conditions.

skills.title: Disease skills
skills.text: Consider possible causes, distinguish relevant clinical signs, and suggest confirmatory testing.

loop.skillsNote: These skills are being refined before expert review and field testing. They are development capabilities, not evidence of clinical accuracy.

together.title: RAG and loop agents are not alternatives
together.text: The two ideas sit together. A loop agent can use retrieval repeatedly, consulting the knowledge base once, assessing, and consulting it again with a sharper question. ShrimpPulse 4.0 keeps the reviewed knowledge base at the centre and adds the ability to go around the loop when a single retrieval is not enough.

boundaries.title: What ShrimpPulse does not do
items: It does not automatically learn from every conversation. Improvements come from structured feedback and deliberate updates to the knowledge base and skills.
It does not continuously browse the internet. Answers are grounded in the curated knowledge base.
It does not have live regulatory updates. Regulatory guidance and real-time policy updates are longer-term ambitions, not current features.
It does not replace a veterinarian, a laboratory, or the regulations that apply to antimicrobial use.
